assumptions: The `callback` service is the running local app on http://127.0.0.1:8001 exposing the action_callback routes (/email/action, /actions/signed, /slack/*), and the harness can restart it.

Because the governed write ships DARK (SandboxInvoiceWriteAdapter, no live writer), 'paid exactly once' / 'no payment effect' are exercised as the single governed-write effect being claimed exactly once against the dark adapter and its ledger, not as a real bank/AP payment.

The three edited files map to the committed governed invoice-write suites eval/tests/test_p4_governed_write_route.py (production entry point) and eval/tests/test_p4_governed_invoice_write.py (execution boundary); these embed the persisted-state oracles (effect_grants counts, security_events, witness rows).

The .venv and pytest-canonical.ini are present and the canonical suite passes on the base tree.
unresolved_questions: The acceptance criteria say an invoice is 'paid', but the shipped code performs RAISE_INVOICE against a dark sandbox adapter (live supervised write is deferred to P12). Is 'paid exactly once' meant to be verified against a real payment effect, or is proving the governed-write effect is claimed exactly once against the dark adapter the intended scope for U-042?

The live governed-approval callback path (/slack/actions -> handle_governed_write_callback) requires a valid Slack signing secret and a signed governed token, which cannot be produced without secrets. As a result the deepest AC behaviours are verified via the hermetic pytest suites rather than over HTTP against the running service; is an end-to-end HTTP exercise of a genuine approval in scope, and if so what signed-fixture affordance is available?

No dedicated test was found that restarts the callback process, re-delivers a previously-consumed approval, and asserts it is refused as already-consumed. AC 'approval survives a restart' is currently only inferable from the durable PK(tenant,action_id) claim; should a true process-restart-then-replay scenario be added once a signed-approval fixture is available?

'What is already covered' and the builder's actual diff were not provided, so scenarios are grounded on the acceptance criteria and the current implementation rather than on the specific lines changed; some may duplicate existing coverage.

The builder-changed file src/freight_recon/carrier_invoice_write.py named in the diff does not exist at that path in the working tree (only eval/tests/test_p4_governed_invoice_write.py matches *invoice_write*); the invoice-write operation typing appears to live in freight_operations.py / effect_boundary.py. The mapping of that changed filename to the current module layout should be confirmed before trusting file-scoped coverage.

action_callback._maybe_handle_governed_write_approval adds explicit fail-closed refusals (ROUTE_NOT_CONFIGURED, NO_STORED_CHANNEL_RECEIPT, CHANNEL_RECEIPT_MISMATCH) that are HTTP-transport-level and have no clearly citeable U-042 acceptance criterion and no approved command to drive the live callback server with a validly-signed governed token; these fail-closed paths are currently unverifiable with the given toolset and no AC promises the channel-receipt binding — flagging rather than inventing a requirement.

No acceptance criterion among the five given covers the 'operator without approval authority is refused' path at the governed-write route specifically beyond S4; if a distinct authority-tier (approval_required vs actor-allowlist) is intended, it is not expressed in the ACs shown.

raw.title: The consumption boundary re-proves the approval->operation lineage independently
raw.purpose: Prove that even a caller bypassing the signed envelope cannot pair a foreign approval identity with a different operation: a substituted approval_id is refused with GovernedWriteIntentRefused and no write, and every binding (approval_id, work_item, pipeline, capability, idempotency_key, revision) is independently load-bearing in approval_operation_mismatch.
raw.rationale: The consumer is separately reachable, so its own re-proof of the lineage is the last barrier against paying under an approval the human never granted for this exact operation.
raw.generating_risk: A foreign approval could be paired with a different operation at the separately-reachable consumer and pay under an approval the human never granted.
raw.requirement_reference: no payment effect occurs without a recorded approval
raw.isolation_note: Committed pytest tests (tmp_path DB + pure-predicate parametrization); no shared state; no cleanup required.

persisted_state_checks.description: a GovernedWriteIntentRefused event persists and writes==0 when a foreign approval is paired with the operation; each substituted binding yields a non-empty mismatch
persisted_state_checks.oracle: embedded test asserts GovernedWriteIntentRefused recorded, writes==0, and approval_operation_mismatch != '' for every substituted field
